articles.name: Announcing the Universal Connector as an external content source for use across knowledge experiences
articles.title: Announcing the Universal Connector as an external content source for use across knowledge experiences
articles.body:
We’re excited to announce the general availability of the Universal Connector as a knowledge source. You can now connect API-based knowledge sources to your Zendesk account with an API key, and make that content available wherever external content is used.

This announcement answers the following questions:

  • What's changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What's changing?

You can now connect REST/JSON knowledge sources to Zendesk Knowledge Graph through a configurable Universal Connector, without requiring a dedicated integration.

Admins can provide an API key and tailor the connection to their source by configuring the API endpoint, request details, response-field mappings, and pagination. This makes it possible to bring knowledge from internal, niche, or custom-built systems into Zendesk.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

The Universal Connector is generally available. Create a Universal Connector connection, add your API key, and configure how Zendesk retrieves and maps content from your REST/JSON source. See Connecting external content using the universal knowledge connector.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Can I automate the CSV export to my AI agent reporting dashboard?
articles.title: Can I automate the CSV export to my AI agent reporting dashboard?
articles.body:
Question

I use the AI agent reporting dashboard and want to automate access to reporting data instead of downloading the Export CSV file manually.

I want to use this data for recurring analysis and reporting, such as sending aggregated AI agent metrics to another tool or service.

What options are available for retrieving this data automatically? For example:

  • Can I schedule CSV exports on a daily or weekly basis?
  • Is there an API that provides the same reporting data available through the dashboard export?
  • Is there another recommended way to access AI agent reporting data programmatically?

Answer

Yes. You can use the Data Export API to export AI agent reporting data including conversation-level detail as JSON files from a secured API endpoint.

Important notes:

  • The Data Export API updates once per day at midnight UTC (Coordinated Universal Time)
  • Requests to Data Export API endpoints use the same account-wide Zendesk API rate limit as other API traffic
  • When calling the Data Export API endpoint https://yoursubdomain.zendesk.com/ai-agents/api/data-export/v3/get-signed-urls you must pass the request headers botId, organizationId, authorization, and date. Use the generated token for the authorization header. You can only pass one date value
  • The returned signed file URLs from the Data Export API endpoint don't need the API token. The signature in the URL query string is the authentication
  • The returned file URL is a temporary signed link that expires one day after the request date. You must call the endpoint again to get a fresh link if it expires
  • Historical data is available back to January 1, 2024. Anything older requires contacting Zendesk Customer Support
  • Generating the API token and finding the org ID both require admin access
  • The export for a date only includes conversations that ended on the date specified based on UTC (Coordinated Universal Time)

articles.name: Inline images in Knowledge articles display as broken across all browsers
articles.title: Inline images in Knowledge articles display as broken across all browsers
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

Inline images in knowledge base articles display as broken links for all users, or don't display for anonymous users or end users.

This problem occurs when an article contains inline image attachments from another article that is:

  • Restricted to a specific group of users
  • In draft status
  • In archived status

Due to any of these reasons, the image displays as a broken link, followed by the image name:

Resolution steps

To fix this issue, follow the step corresponding to the article status:

  • If the article is restricted to a specific group of users, update the restriction settings
  • If the article is in draft status, publish the article
  • If the article is in an archived status, restore the article

Alternatively, download the attachments and upload them individually to each article or use the knowledge media library. This is the recommended approach.

To identify the location of the attachment in the original article:

  1. Inspect the individual element in the browser console and copy its unique numerical ID

  2. Run the following API call for article attachments:

    https://{{subdomain}}.zendesk.com/api/v2/help_center/articles/attachments/123456789.json

    Replace subdomain with yoursubdomain and the unique ID value with that of the original article inline attachment.

You'll receive the following response that retrieves the original article source:

{
"article_attachment": {
"id": 123456789,
"url": "https://subdomain.zendesk.com/api/v2/help_center/articles/attachments/123456789",
"article_id": 360001328736,
"display_file_name": "Screen Shot 2020-02.png",
"file_name": "Screen_Shot_2020-02.png",
"content_url": "https://subdomain.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/1233456789/Screen_Shot_2020-02.png",
"relative_path": "/hc/article_attachments/123456789/Screen_Shot_2020-02.png",
"content_type": "image/png",
"size": 218402,
"inline": true,
"created_at": "2020-02-30T16:30:33Z",
"updated_at": "2020-02-30T16:45:03Z"
}
}

After you identify the article's unique ID, add it to any knowledge base article editor and this returns the article, for example:

https://{{subdomain}}.zendesk.com/knowledge/articles/360001328736/en-us?brand_id=3149466

For more information, see Working with articles in the knowledge base.

articles.name: Announcing the general availability of multi-recipient email tickets
articles.title: Announcing the general availability of multi-recipient email tickets
articles.body:
Beginning September 1st, the multi-recipient email ticket feature will move from open EAP to general availability (GA) and become available to all customers. This new feature, controlled through a setting on the Email Settings page in Admin Center, improves team collaboration on tickets by ensuring a ticket is created for each support address on an inbound email ticket.

This announcement answers the following questions:

  • What's changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What's changing?

Zendesk is releasing a new setting that creates a ticket for each support address included on an email ticket. For example, an email sent to it@company.zendesk.com and hr@company.zendesk.com creates two tickets: one assigned to the IT support address and another to HR support, ensuring efficient collaboration on multi-department requests.

Additionally, when those tickets are created, they'll be linked through a unique field ID named multi-recipient email id, and will include a private note at the beginning of the ticket notifying agents that it is the result of the multi-recipient email ticket workflow. 

For more information, see Turning on multi-recipient email tickets.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

This new feature lets customers communicate in more complex ways and collaborate across teams more seamlessly. 

What do I need to do?

No action is needed. This is a new setting available to all customers in Support.

If a customer was a part of the EAP and had the EAP setting enabled on its Support instance, no change is needed. The setting value will be carried over to GA.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Announcing new Google Sheets actions for action flows
articles.title: Announcing new Google Sheets actions for action flows

By expanding the available actions in Google Sheets, Zendesk helps teams create more connected and efficient workflows in action flows.

articles.name: Editing and managing custom agents (EAP)
articles.title: Editing and managing custom agents (EAP)
articles.body:
Custom agents can be updated at any time.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus

Summary: ◀▼

You can edit, activate, deactivate, and delete custom agents that automate tasks using AI and predefined workflows. Activate agents when ready to use, deactivate them to pause without deleting, and delete agents you no longer need. Managing custom agents helps maintain and update automated customer support processes effectively.

Note: Custom agents are currently in an early access program (EAP). To participate, see Joining the Custom Agents EAP.
Custom agents use a combination of AI, user-defined procedures, and approved articles, tools, and custom actions to automate complex tasks and resolve customer issues. After custom agents are created, admins can take the following actions to manage custom agents and maintain their workflows:
  • Editing custom agents
  • Activating and deactivating custom agents
  • Deleting custom agents
Related resources:
  • Understanding custom agents in Zendesk
  • Creating and using custom agents in Zendesk

Editing custom agents

Custom agents can be updated at any time.

To edit a custom agent
  1. In Admin Center, click AI in the sidebar, then select Agent builder > Custom agents.
  2. Next to the custom agent you want to edit, click the options menu () and select Edit.
  3. Make the necessary changes.
  4. Click Save.

Activating and deactivating custom agents

Custom agents are inactive by default. When you're ready to use them, activate them. If you need to modify a custom agent or temporarily don't need it, you can deactivate custom agents. They can be re-activated at any time. If you want to permanently remove a custom agent, you can delete it.
Note: Action flows that have a hand off step connected to a custom agent will break if the custom agent is deactivated.
To activate or deactivate a custom agent
  1. In Admin Center, click AI in the sidebar, then select Agent builder > Custom agents.
  2. Next to the custom agent, click the options menu () and select Activate or Deactivate.

Deleting custom agents

If you no longer need a custom agent, you can delete it. If you might need the custom agent again in the future, you can deactivate it instead.

To delete a custom agent
  1. In Admin Center, click AI in the sidebar, then select Agent builder > Custom agents.
  2. Next to the custom agent, click the options menu () and select Delete.
  3. In the confirmation dialog, click Delete.

articles.name: Can I use AI suggestions to generate use cases for advanced email AI agents?
articles.title: Can I use AI suggestions to generate use cases for advanced email AI agents?
articles.body:
Question

I can't generate any suggestions for my email AI agent, and the error appears with ai agent does not have any conversations.

Can I use AI Suggestions to generate use cases for advanced email AI agents?

Answer

Yes. The ai agent does not have any conversations error is misleading. It's tied to the source you picked rather than to the channel or bot generation. With the default Report preset > Quick, the Source defaults to This AI agent and includes only messages that were classified as not understood.

This method queries only for conversations carrying not understood conversations, and when it finds none, it returns the ai agent does not have any conversations error. A bot with plenty of traffic but few not understood messages may encounter this error. A topic needs at least 5 conversations before it surfaces as a suggestion, so a small sample can return nothing even when the import succeeds.

For AI agents connected to email channels, switch the Report preset from Quick to Custom and set Source to Zendesk Support. That pulls historical email tickets from your Zendesk account that includes public comments only, no private notes, excludes messaging tickets, and you can raise the Conversations sample to 1000 or 2000 to include more tickets.

articles.name: Announcing notifications and settings for automated resolutions and resolution allowances
articles.title: Announcing notifications and settings for automated resolutions and resolution allowances
articles.body:
Starting September 1, 2026, all new and existing Zendesk customers on any plan consuming automated resolutions and resolution allowances will start receiving these new usage notifications via email and see in-product notification banners. The new notification types include first use notification, forecasted possible overage notifications, and limit exceeded notifications.

To help you manage automated resolutions or resolution allowance usage alerts, you can configure the emails notifications that admins receive to track usage. These notification settings work for usage traced by the Automated resolutions dashboard as well as usage tracked by the Resolution allowance and Resolution usage dashboards.  

This announcement contains these sections:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing? 

In addition to the new notification types for first use notification, forecasted possible overage notifications, and limit exceeded notifications, Admin Center has a new Manage notifications page you can use to control which admins are notified by email when resolution usage occurs.

You can configure email notifications to be sent when the following usage events occur for automated resolutions:

  • Approaching limit: Usage reaches a certain percentage of your overall resolution allowance. Options you can set range from 50% to 90%. 
  • Reached limit: Usage reaches 100%.
  • Exceeding limit: Usage goes beyond 100%. Email notifications are sent at intervals of 10%.
  • Forecast: When the forecast indicates account usage may exceed the allowance.

For each notification type, you can configure which admins in your account will receive the email notifications. See Managing usage notifications for automated resolutions and resolution allowances for details.

Why is Zendesk making this change? 

By providing new notification types customers get additional proactive usage alerts to avoid unexpected overage invoices. Additionally, Zendesk is introducing recipient and limit configuration options for these notifications so they reach the right team members within a support team, avoiding bill issues or service disruptions. This functionality also allows admins to switch off notifications for certain team members to prevent alert fatigue.

What do I need to do? 

No action is required. Once this feature is rolled out to your account, you can configure which admins in your account receive email notifications for automated resolution usage. See Managing usage notifications for automated resolutions and resolution allowances. All your admins are included by default.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Announcing human-in-the-loop and multi-step sequential approvals
articles.title: Announcing human-in-the-loop and multi-step sequential approvals
articles.body:
Zendesk is pleased to announce two new capabilities for approvals: automated human-in-the-loop approval processes and multiple sequential approval requests on a ticket.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

With this release, admins can create two new kinds of approval workflows.

Human-in-the-loop approvals in action flows

Admins can create action flows that send approval requests, pause until a response is received, and then resume automatically following steps based on the response. This is referred to as human-in-the-loop automated approval requests. This allows automated workflows to mirror complex organizational logic, ensuring that critical approval decisions are made by the right stakeholders before the process continues. For example, pausing an automated onboarding process until the appropriate stakeholder approves the request and allows onboarding to continue.

As with all approval requests generated through action flows, you can specify a single individual or use variables to define who the approver should be for automatically-generated approval request in cases where it's dynamic. Variables come from previous steps in an acton flow, such as looking up a user and retrieving their manager's ID.

Multi-step sequential approvals

Multiple, sequential approval requests are also possible now. This can be automated through action flows, using multiple send approval request steps configured to wait for a response, as described above, or manually within the Agent Workspace by creating multiple approval requests to a ticket after the previous one is completed. Multiple approval requests allow teams to build sequential approval workflows for more complex processes, and they reduce the manual effort required to follow-up and hand-off tickets. 

For example, service teams can automate procurement processes and enable multiple approvers across finance and IT organizations to make a decision before a final vendor contract agreement is assigned.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Zendesk has heard your feedback on end-to-end automations needing to wait for approval requests to complete and to have multiple approvals in the same workflow. The functionality in this release is designed for approval workflows that accurately align with actual operational procedures, ensuring decisions are made by the appropriate stakeholders at the optimal time in the process.

Benefits include:

  • Automation: Now, a single action flow can cover end-to-end business processes, such as onboarding, expense reimbursement, and contract reviews.
  • Waiting for approval response: Allows end-to-end action flows to wait, and then continue based on the approver's decision.
  • Multiple, sequential approvals: Allows complex approval steps within a single action flow.

What do I need to do?

This enhancements are available to all accounts with access to action flows and approval requests. To get started, you can create or update action flows to include the Send approval request step and configure the step's behavior to Continue immediately or Wait for a response.

Existing action flows with a Send approval request step default to continuing immediately. If you want to change this to a human-in-the-loop workflow, edit the step's behavior to wait for a response. All new Send approval request steps default to waiting for a response.

For more information, see Creating human-in-the-loop automated approval workflows.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Can AI agents answer general knowledge questions?
articles.title: Can AI agents answer general knowledge questions?
articles.body:
Question

Can my AI agent answer general knowledge questions or widely known facts that aren’t included in my connected knowledge sources?

Answer

No. AI agents in Zendesk answer questions using the use cases you configure and the knowledge sources you connect to your account.

If a user asks a general knowledge question, such as “What is the capital of France?”, and that information isn’t available in the connected knowledge sources, the AI agent typically won’t answer it as a supported fact. Instead, it may fall back to another configured behavior, such as the Technical Error Reply use case, or another response path it determines is more appropriate.

This behavior is intentional. The AI agent focuses on content from connected knowledge sources, including your Zendesk Help Center and external knowledge sources. The AI agent stays grounded in your approved support content rather than act as a general-purpose knowledge bot. It works best when answering questions about your products and features, guiding common troubleshooting steps, and surfacing relevant help center content from connected and accessible sources.

For more information, see Connecting knowledge sources to power generative replies in AI agents.

articles.title: Release notes through 2026-08-28

articles.name: Announcing a new way to manage light agent permissions in non-Enterprise plans
articles.title: Announcing a new way to manage light agent permissions in non-Enterprise plans
articles.body:
Zendesk is introducing a new way for non-Enterprise plan admins to manage and view roles in Admin Center. Admins can now manage light agent permissions directly in Admin Center, replacing the previous settings experience in Agent Workspace. This update creates a consistent, role-based experience across all plan tiers and supports Zendesk’s ongoing investment in custom roles.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What's changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What's changing?

  • A new Roles link is added under Admin Center > People > Team in Admin Center for non-Enterprise plans, and is now searchable from the Admin Center Search field.
  • The "Light agent access" section is removed from Workspaces > Agent Interface. In its place, admins will see a note directing them to manage light agent access through the new Roles page.
  • On non-Enterprise plans, the Roles page displays three roles: Admin, Contributor, and Light Agent.
  • Only the Light Agent role is editable on these plans. Admins can configure:
    • Ticket access — which tickets light agents can view
    • Explore access — whether light agents can access Explore
  • All other permissions on the light agent role remain enabled and greyed out.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

This update is part of Zendesk's broader initiative to bring consistency across all plan tiers, replacing fragmented, plan-specific settings with a single, consistent roles-based experience. For non-Enterprise plans, this means light agent management now lives in the same place it does for Enterprise customers, making administration more intuitive and reducing confusion when comparing plans or considering an upgrade. It also lays the architectural groundwork for extending fuller custom role capabilities to lower plans in the future.

What do I need to do?

No action is required. Existing light agent configurations will carry over automatically, and admins on non-Enterprise plans will see the new Roles page appear in Admin Center as the rollout reaches their account. Once available, admins can go to Admin Center > People > Team > Roles to view and manage light agent ticket and Explore access.

articles.title: Service Incident - August 19, 2026 - Support | Multiple Pods - App errors and timeouts
articles.body:
Summary

On August 19, 2026 from 6:27 UTC to 8:09 UTC, some Support customers using third party apps experienced errors and difficulties accessing those applications. The issue affected customers in several pods and resulted in 503 errors or timeouts.

Timeline

August 19, 2026 08:00 AM UTC | 1:00AM PT
 
We’re investigating an issue affecting third-party app functionality, where some customers may be unable to use certain apps or may encounter errors and timeouts. Our teams have observed that service is now operating normally. Please refresh your browser and check whether the issue has been resolved on your end. Thank you for your patience as we worked through this.
 
 
August 19, 2026 08:33 AM UTC | 1:33AM PT
 
We’re happy to report that the issue affecting third-party app functionality has been fully resolved and service has been restored. We appreciate your understanding and cooperation throughout this incident.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a front-end change that unintentionally deprecated a feature flag which controlled routing for requests from applications, causing those requests to result in errors.

Resolution

To fix this issue, the feature flag was manually re-enabled, which restored application request routing to its intended path.

Remediation Items

  1. Change feature flag deprecation controls.
  2. Revisit and improve feature flag adjustment permissions.
  3. Improve runbook for similar deploys to reduce response time in similar scenarios.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Managing usage notifications for automated resolutions and resolution allowances
articles.title: Managing usage notifications for automated resolutions and resolution allowances
articles.body:
To help you manage automated resolutions, you can configure the email notifications that admins receive to track automated resolution usage and resolution allowances. These notification settings work for usage tracked by theAutomated resolutions dashboardas well as usage tracked by theResolution allowanceandResolution usagedashboards.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus

Summary: ◀▼

Set up email notifications for automated resolutions and resolution allowances. Control which admins receive the notifications. Notifications help you stay informed about usage thresholds and forecasted overages, preventing unexpected charges.

Location: Admin Center > Account > Usage > Manage notifications

To help you manage automated resolutions, you can configure the email notifications that admins receive to track automated resolution usage and resolution allowances. These notification settings work for usage tracked by the Automated resolutions dashboard as well as usage tracked by the Resolution allowance and Resolution usage dashboards.

This article contains these sections:

  • About configuring usage notification emails
  • Accessing the Manage notifications page
  • Setting email notifications
  • Adding or removing admins from the recipient list

Related articles/

  • Monitoring usage on the automated resolution platform
  • Managing resolution allowances
  • Managing resolution usage

About configuring usage notification emails

You can configure email notifications to be sent when the following usage allowance events occur for automated resolutions:

  • Approaching limit: Usage reaches a certain percentage of your overall resolution allowance. Options you can set range from 50% to 90%.
  • Reached limit: Usage reaches 100%.
  • Exceeding limit: Usage goes beyond 100%. Email notifications are sent at intervals of 10%.
  • Forecast: When the forecast indicates account usage may exceed the allowance.

For each notification type, you can configure which admins in your account will receive the email notifications.

Accessing the Manage notifications page

Use the Manage notifications page in Admin Center to set up email notifications for automated resolution usage.

To open the Manage notifications page

  • In Admin Center, click Account in the sidebar, then select Usage > Manage notifications.

    The Manage notifications page appears with a list of notification types. Use this page to configure recipients for each notification type.

Setting email notifications

For each notification type, you can configure which admins will receive an email notification. By default all admins in your account are included in the recipient list.

To set email notifications

  1. In Admin Center, click Account in the sidebar, then select Usage > Manage notifications.
  2. Click one of the following notification types to expand it: Approaching limit, Reached limit, Exceeding limit, or Forecast
  3. If you're setting the Approaching limit, click Send notification when usage reaches and select the desired percentage.

    You can set email notifications for one of the following: 50%, 60%, 70%, 80% or 90%.

    This setting applies only to the approaching limit. It's not applicable to the other notification types.

  4. Select the recipients to receive the email notification. See Adding or removing admins from the recipient list.
  5. When you’ve finished selecting recipients, click Save.

Adding or removing admins from the recipient list

For each notification type, you can select which admins will receive the notification. By default, all the current admins in your account are automatically included as recipients for all notification types, but any new admins you add going forward will need to be added manually. Only admins can be recipients of resolution allowance notifications.

Removing recipients

You can remove admins from the list, but at minimum, the account owner and at least one billing admin must be recipients.

To remove an admin from the list

  1. In Admin Center, click Account in the sidebar, then select Usage > Manage notifications.
  2. Click to expand the notification type you want to update.
  3. In the Recipient list, locate the admin you want to remove from the list.
  4. Click the options menu icon () next to the recipient and select Remove recipient.

  5. Continue to remove additional admins as needed.
  6. Click Save.

Adding recipients to a notification type

In some cases, you may want to add a previously-removed admin back into the recipient list or include a new admin you’re added recently to your account. New admins are not added automatically as notification recipients.

To add an admin to the list

  1. In Admin Center, click Account in the sidebar, then select Usage > Manage notifications.
  2. Click to expand the notification type you want to update.
  3. Scroll to the bottom of the recipient list and click Add recipient.

  4. Search to locate the admin you want to add, then click Add recipient.

    You can add one recipient at a time.

  5. Click Save.

Adding a recipient to all notifications

In some cases you might want to quickly add an admin to all notifications at once.

To add an admin to all notifications at once

  1. In Admin Center, click Account in the sidebar, then select Usage > Manage notifications.
  2. Click the Action menu at the top of the Manage notifications page.

  3. Select Add recipient to all notifications.
  4. Search to locate the admin you want to add, then click Add recipient.

    A confirmation message appears that says: "A recipient was added to all notifications."

articles.name: Understanding the difference between looking up and searching for custom object records in action flows
articles.title: Understanding the difference between looking up and searching for custom object records in action flows
articles.body:
Action flowsare user-defined automated workflows that can perform actions in Zendesk and connected external systems. Within action flows, there are two ways to retrieve custom object records: theLookup custom object recordstep and theSearch for custom object recordstep. While both return information about custom object records, it's important to understand when to use each of these actions.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

You can retrieve custom object records in action flows using two methods: lookup by record ID for specific records linked to tickets or users, and search by object type with filter conditions, search terms, and sorting options to find multiple relevant records. Use lookup when you have the record ID, and search when you need to find records based on characteristics or keywords.

Action flows are user-defined automated workflows that can perform actions in Zendesk and connected external systems. Within action flows, there are two ways to retrieve custom object records: the Lookup custom object record step and the Search for custom object record step. While both return information about custom object records, it's important to understand when to use each of these actions.

The Lookup custom object record action requires a record ID as input and returns data only about that particular record. This action is commonly used when a record is related to a ticket, user, or other object that has already come up in a previous step of the action flow and the ID can be entered as a variable from a previous step.

The Search for custom object record action takes an object type and conditions as input rather than an ID. This makes it possible to return one or more relevant custom object records based on other characteristics of the records. When configuring the search conditions for this action, you can specify the following:
  • Filter conditions: The characteristics matching records must have, in the format of Category | Operator | Value. Conditions can be nested up to three layers deep.
  • Search term: The word or phrase is searched against all text-based fields in the records. Separate multiple words with spaces.
  • Sort order: Sort the matching records by name, when it was created, or when it was last updated. If sort order isn't specified, it defaults to relevance.
  • Page size: Specify the number of records to return per page.
  • Sort by: Sort the matching records by ascending or descending order. Available only when sort order is specified.

articles.name: Setting up Contact Center on a Zendesk-managed AWS account
articles.title: Setting up Contact Center on a Zendesk-managed AWS account
articles.body:
Use this guide when setting up Zendesk Contact Center for a customer where Zendesk provisions and manages the AWS account. In this deployment model, Zendesk and Zendesk partners complete the customer-specific Amazon Connect and Zendesk configuration described below. Some steps require access that only Zendesk employees have; those steps are marked clearly.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

This guide helps you set up Contact Center on a Zendesk-managed AWS account, from AWS account provisioning to telephony testing. You’ll confirm federated access, create a test user, claim a test phone number, validate inbound and outbound calling, and check that call recordings and transcripts appear on tickets. It also covers optional cleanup of test resources.

Use this guide when setting up Zendesk Contact Center for a customer where Zendesk provisions and manages the AWS account. In this deployment model, Zendesk and Zendesk partners complete the customer-specific Amazon Connect and Zendesk configuration described below. Some steps require access that only Zendesk employees have; those steps are marked clearly.

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Administrator access to the Zendesk account and its valid subdomain, such as example.zendesk.com
  • The customer technical contact and the required AWS Region, telephony, and SSO details
  • A Zendesk contact who can provision the AWS account and perform internal Monitor or Contact Center Admin actions
  • An active Contact Center license

This article contains the following topics:

  • Step 1: Zendesk provisions the AWS account
  • Step 2: Configure Connect access and validate settings
  • Step 3: Test telephony capabilities
  • Step 4: Clean up (Optional)

Related articles:

  • About AWS services in Contact Center
  • Accessing Amazon Connect and AWS Console from Contact Center

Step 1: Zendesk provisions the AWS account

Important: The actions in this step require a Zendesk employee with access to the relevant internal provisioning and administration systems.

Start by providing the following information to your Zendesk contact:

  • Zendesk account name, ID, and valid subdomain, such as example.zendesk.com
  • Customer technical contact details
  • Intended Amazon Connect Region
  • Required telephony and SSO configuration details
  • Preferred Amazon Connect instance name

Your Zendesk contact will provision or associate the AWS account, create or identify the Amazon Connect instance, complete the required internal account and SKU-linking steps, and confirm when the account is ready.

Step 2: Configure Connect access and validate settings

In this section, you'll configure a test user, claim a test phone number, and optionally enable outbound dialing in your Amazon Connect instance.

2.1 Configure test user

After Zendesk confirms that the AWS account and Amazon Connect instance are ready, create a test user so you can validate agent access.

To configure a test user

  1. Navigate to the Overview page and click the Log in for emergency access link:

  2. From the Amazon Connect Dashboard, navigate to User Management and click Add new users:

  3. From the Add user page:

    • Enter the First name.

    • Enter the Last name.

    • Enter the Login. This must match the corresponding Zendesk user's primary email address exactly, including capitalization.

    • Select the Security profile permissions, such as Admin or Agent.

    • Select a Routing profile, such as Basic Routing Profile.

    • Click Save.

2.2 Claim test phone number

Next, claim a temporary phone number and associate it with the sample inbound flow for testing.

To claim a test phone number

  1. Navigate to the Phone numbers page and click Claim a number:

  2. On the Claim Phone number page:

    • Select Voice as the channel if it isn't already selected by default.

    • Click the DID tab. Toll-free is also supported, but DIDs are cheaper for testing.

    • Select the country.

    • Select an available phone number from the list.

    • Select the Sample inbound flow (first contact experience) contact flow supplied by Amazon Connect.

    • Click Save.

2.3 Enable outbound dialing (Optional)

If outbound calling is part of your validation plan, assign the test number as the caller ID for the basic queue.

To enable outbound dialing

  1. To test outbound calling, navigate to the Queues page and click BasicQueue:

  2. On the Edit BasicQueue page, scroll down to Settings - optional.

  3. Search for and select the phone number you claimed in Step 2.2, then click Save.

Step 3: Test telephony capabilities

In this section, you'll verify federated access, then test inbound and outbound calling.

3.1 Test federated access to Amazon Connect and AWS

Verify that the Zendesk account provides the expected federated access to both Amazon Connect and the AWS Management Console.

To test federated access to Amazon Connect and AWS

  1. Log out of the AWS Management Console unless you're using an incognito browser tab.

  2. Log out of and back into your Zendesk account.

  3. Navigate to the Contact Center configuration console.

  4. From the Overview page:

    1. Click the Amazon Connect Dashboard link to validate federated access to the Amazon Connect Dashboard.

    2. Click the AWS Console link to verify access to the AWS Management Console.

For example:

3.2 Test inbound calling

Use the test number to place an inbound call, confirm that it reaches an available agent, and verify the resulting ticket data.

To test inbound calling

  1. From the Support page in Zendesk, click the user icon in the top-right corner and select Online to make the agent available:

  2. Call the phone number claimed in Step 2.2. Follow the menu options offered by Amazon Connect to be placed in a queue and transferred to an agent.

  3. Accept the incoming call and close the notification:

  4. Speak a few words to validate the recording and call transcription, then end the call.

  5. Click Finish wrap-up to close the Amazon Connect contact:

  6. Wait a few minutes to verify that the call recording and transcription are appended to the ticket. This may take up to four to five minutes:

3.3 Test outbound calling

After inbound calling is validated, place an outbound call to confirm that the agent calling workflow is configured correctly.

To test outbound calling

  1. From the Support page in Zendesk, click the phone icon. Enter a phone number and click Call:

  2. When the call is connected and your phone rings, click End to hang up.

  3. Click Finish wrap-up in the pop-up window to close the contact.

Step 4: Clean up (Optional)

When testing is complete, remove the temporary resources and test data that are no longer needed.

To clean up the test resources

  1. Clear the Outbound caller ID number from the BasicProfile routing profile in Amazon Connect.

  2. Release the phone number claimed in Step 2.2 because it was intended only for testing.

  3. Delete any tickets created in Zendesk during testing and validation.

articles.name: Announcing the general availability of voice AI agents
articles.title: Announcing the general availability of voice AI agents
articles.body:
Today, we're announcing that Zendesk voice AI agents are generally available. Voice AI agents are a native, agentic automation solution for the voice channel. They enable natural, real-time phone conversations, handling calls end to end and transferring customers to human agents when needed.

When a call is transferred, the associated ticket includes the conversation history and context, helping the human agent continue the conversation without asking the customer to repeat themselves

Following the early access program (EAP) that began in February 2026, voice AI agents are now available to all eligible customers, with no sign-up required.

Note: Voice AI agents are not available with Talk Partner Edition. Support for Zendesk Contact Center is planned for a future release.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What's changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What's changing?

All Zendesk customers with voice (Talk) can now build and assign generative voice AI agents to Zendesk voice phone lines, automating routine phone support and handling more sophisticated workflows powered by generative procedures, integrations, and real-time data access.

Key capabilities

  • End-to-end voice automation, from greeting and intent capture through resolution and wrap-up.
  • Natural, real-time conversations that let customers speak freely and receive immediate responses.
  • Native voice integration, so you can assign AI agents directly to your existing phone lines without making telephony changes.
  • Seamless escalation to human agents through omnichannel or native voice routing. The associated ticket includes the full transcript, AI-generated summary, and detected intent, so agents can start with context.
  • Generative procedures and actions, including API calls, database lookups, ticket field and tag updates, SMS messages, public email replies, and ending calls.
  • Browser-based testing widget that lets you test an AI agent end to end from the AI agents workspace without placing a real call.
  • AI agent call recordings posted to the associated ticket, where they can be played alongside the transcript and summary.
  • Multilingual support for conversations in 53 languages, with language-specific voices, locales, and accents.
  • Ticket for every call connected to an AI agent, including a transcript and summary for tracking, reporting, and transfers.

Availability and pricing

Voice AI agents are available to Zendesk customers with voice. Usage is billed based on:

  • Automated resolutions: You pay only for confirmed resolutions. See About automated resolution tiers and Managing resolution allowances.
  • Voice minutes and AI agent connection charges: Standard telephony rates apply, and there is also a charge for the time the AI agent is on the call. See Zendesk Talk number availability and pricing.
  • AI agent call recordings: Recordings are billed per minute at the standard call recording rate and are visible in your Usage dashboard. You can turn off AI agent call recording in your call recording configuration; transcripts and summaries will still be added to the ticket.

Information for existing EAP participants

Following the rollout, your account will automatically convert to GA. Your billing, setup, and AI agents will remain unchanged, so no action is needed on your part.

We are introducing an upgraded ticket experience aligned with other channels and integrated with AI agent tickets. Although this functionality debuts with GA, existing EAP participants are excluded from the initial release as it may necessitate workflow adjustments. Our team will reach out in the coming weeks to assist you with adopting and leveraging this enhancement.

Important: Voice AI agents are not intended for evaluating or classifying emergency calls, or for emergency dispatch or triage scenarios.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Voice is a high-volume, high-expectation channel. Voice AI agents help teams offer 24/7 phone support, reduce repetitive agent work, and resolve customer requests faster. When human help is needed, agents have the context they need to continue the conversation.

What do I need to do?

  • Get started: See About voice AI agents to understand how voice AI agents work and review best practices.
  • Get building: See Creating an AI agent for voice to build, test, and activate your first voice AI agent.
  • Add languages: See Configuring multi-language support for voice AI agents.
  • Review usage: See Reviewing your voice usage charges.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: What's new in Zendesk: September 2026
articles.title: What's new in Zendesk: September 2026
articles.body:
Click Follow in the What's New section to be notified each month when the What's New is published.

Check out what's new in the last month:

  • Support
  • Accounts and billing
  • AI agents
  • Copilot
  • Objects and business rules
  • Security
  • People
  • Knowledge
  • Messaging
  • Contact Center
  • Voice
  • Analytics
  • Workforce management
  • Quality assurance
  • Apps and integrations

Also don't miss:

  • Zendesk early access programs
  • What's new videos on YouTube

Support

  • Multi-lookup relationship fields allow admins to create ticket fields that connect one ticket to multiple related records, such as users, organizations, assets, and custom objects. This simplifies workflows by enabling automation through action flows and business rules without custom logic. Multi-lookup fields are available on Zendesk Suite Professional and Support Enterprise plans. See Understanding relationship fields and Creating many-to-many relationships in Zendesk.
  • The messaging integration in views improves how messaging activity is represented, updating the Latest Update timestamp more reliably and adding an active conversation indicator. This helps agents prioritize active messaging tickets more effectively with no action required from users. See Accessing and using the Views admin page.
  • AI translations, already available for email, web form, and API, now support conversational channels (live chat and messaging). Translations run in real time so agents and customers can communicate in their own languages during live conversations. See Turning on and off AI translation for ticket conversations. 

  • The notifications list supports additional notifications for email tickets and reopened tickets. Also, agents can configure their own notifications settings in Admin Center. See Managing ticket notification settings in Admin Center. 

  • You can create links to connect directly to specific comments within a ticket and share it with others. Comment links make it easier to share the exact context with teammates, collaborate on complex requests, and reduce the time spent searching through ticket histories. See Linking directly to comments in a ticket. 

  • Enhancements to the unified agent status picker now give admins the ability to hide unnecessary statuses and reorder them to better match agent workflows. This customization improves efficiency by showing only relevant statuses and placing frequently used ones at the top. See Managing the unified agent statuses available to your agents.
  • The audio comments feature for messaging and email tickets introduces an embedded audio recorder in Agent Workspace, allowing agents to record, review, and send audio replies directly within Zendesk. This streamlines workflows, speeds up responses, and enhances accessibility. The feature is enabled by default with an admin setting to control it. See Allowing agents to send audio messages and Receiving and sending audio comments in email and messaging tickets.

Accounts and billing

  • You can view invoice details from the Invoices page in Admin Center. Invoice details include all transactions associated with an invoice, including payments, credit memos, refunds, and write-offs. Each transaction listed includes the transaction type, status, applied amount, and the remaining invoice balance after each transaction. See Managing invoices. 

AI agents

  • Cloning an AI agent now duplicates the AI agent's full configuration, including procedures, actions, knowledge sources, search rules, segments, and personalization settings. This improvement supports sandbox-to-production and sandbox-to-sandbox workflows, ensuring cloned agents behave like the original. See Cloning an AI agent.

  • Admins can set templated opening and closing lines in email responses for AI agents with agentic AI. This allows you to set static, personalized opening and closing lines for AI-generated emails, ensuring brand consistency and predictability. See Configuring an AI agent’s opening and closing lines in email responses.

  • Sources used for AI-generated answers now appear in a separate view. In the Web Widget and on social channels, customers can click to view the sources that an AI agent used to generate a reply, rather than seeing a lists of sources directly in the AI agent's response. This reduces clutter and improves readability for messaging conversations. See Displaying sources for generative replies.

  • Schedules set in Admin Center now apply to AI agents. You can use a schedule to define the business hours, time zones, and holidays that affect escalation workflows for your AI agents. See Checking business hours and agent availability during AI agent conversations.
  • Enhancements to the Resolution usage and Resolution allowance dashboards. You can filter by brand and tier. In addition, on the Resolution usage dashboard, you can also export resolution usage data for any selected date range. See Managing resolution usage and Managing resolution allowances. 

Copilot

  • Merge suggestions are now included at no additional cost for Suite and Support Professional plans and above, helping agents identify and merge related tickets to reduce handling time and duplicate tickets. Usage for this feature is pooled across all agents in an account. See Turning on and configuring AI-generated merge suggestions.

  • Guided onboarding for auto assist is now available. It helps simplifies setup by guiding admins through selecting knowledge sources, enabling access, and publishing AI-generated procedures. This onboarding is available once per account in Admin Center. See Turning on and configuring auto assist.

  • Admin copilot now includes role-based permissions for conversational assistance, allowing control over custom role access. It also features an expanded view for detailed responses and integrates Zendesk QA recommendations for proactive conversation quality improvement. See Managing access to admin copilot conversational assistance and Understanding admin copilot recommendations.

  • The similar tickets feature in the Copilot add-on has been improved with a hybrid retrieval model that combines keyword and semantic matching. This feature now supports all languages and channels to find more relevant past solutions faster. See Turning on similar tickets.
  • Version management for agent copilot and intelligent triage now allows you to inspect, save, compare, and deploy AI-related configurations across sandbox and production environments. This helps keep settings aligned and supports testing in sandbox before production deployment. See Inspecting sandbox and production account configurations.

Objects and business rules

  • An update to action credits usage for native Zendesk actions allows unlimited automation of Zendesk operations, including all standard Zendesk actions and Zendesk-built external actions, without affecting credit usage. Action credits now apply to third-party connectors and custom actions only. See Monitoring the usage of action credits and action flow activity.
  • The AI-powered object builder in admin copilot is now generally available, allowing admins to create and refine custom objects and fields using simple language and AI-generated models. This feature accelerates setup by reducing manual schema design and deployment effort. See Creating custom objects using the AI object builder.
  • Flexible custom object record permissions for light agents and contributors allows admins to configure full object-level and record-level access permissions for the light agent and contributor roles, providing tailored access control and enhanced security. See Configuring permissions to access custom object records.

Security

  • The Manage APIs permission introduces granular control for Enterprise plan admins to delegate API and OAuth client management to developers without full admin rights. It enables creation, editing, deletion of API tokens, OAuth clients, Conversations API credentials, and viewing API analytics. This enhances security by adhering to least privilege principles and improves operational efficiency. See Creating and editing custom roles.
  • Access log webhooks enables admins to receive access log events in near real time at a customer-configured HTTPS endpoint, simplifying SIEM integration for customers with the Advanced Data Privacy and Protection add-on. This includes webhook subscriptions, batching, retries, and delivery receipts to enhance security workflows and reduce operational overhead. See Using the access log to monitor agent activity.
  • Custom redaction suggestions enables organizations with the Advanced Data Privacy and Protection add-on to automatically detect unique types of personally identifiable information (PII) in tickets using custom regular expressions (RegEx). This helps protect sensitive data, reduce manual effort, and improve compliance by highlighting data for redaction in the Zendesk Agent Workspace. See Turning on and configuring redaction suggestions.
  • The password security level update removes legacy Low, Medium, and High password levels for team members, migrating accounts to the Recommended level or updated Custom policies with stronger requirements. Passwords must be at least 12 characters and cannot resemble email addresses. Team members will be prompted to reset passwords after migration starting August 17, 2026. See Changing the password security level.
  • The 12-hour session limit is being enforced for all team members to enhance account security by preventing indefinitely active sessions. This change rolls out in two phases based on current inactivity settings, with forced sign-outs for long-running sessions. Admins can review and adjust session expiration settings to comply with the new policy. See Customizing the inactivity session time-out period.

People

  • The Team Member visibility change corrects a permissions issue in Admin Center for Enterprise customers by restricting agents with only Manage end users permission from seeing or accessing the Team Members page. This fix ensures access aligns with assigned permissions, requiring no action from users.

Knowledge

  • The following knowledge connectors are now available to connect as external knowledge sources to your Zendesk account. Content from external knowledge sources is available wherever external content is used.

    • Salesforce
    • Hubspot

    See Connecting external knowledge sources to your Zendesk account.

  • The web crawler advanced URL filters and custom scheduler enhance crawl coverage and control by allowing up to 500 start URLs per crawler, multi-domain crawling, customizable refresh schedules, and up to 500 include and exclude filter rules. These improvements help target relevant content and improve search and AI responses. See Creating URL filters to scope website syncs.

Messaging

  • Brand filtering in the messaging Web Widget allows end users to see only conversations associated with the brand they are currently engaging with, reducing confusion and improving conversation management. This filter applies to the last 100 conversations and requires multi-conversation support and multiple brands in the account. Mobile SDK support is coming soon. See Turning on brand filtering.
  • WhatsApp business-scoped user IDs (BSUIDs) is now generally available in Zendesk and the Sunshine Conversations API, enabling support for WhatsApp users identified by BSUIDs instead of phone numbers as Meta rolls out WhatsApp usernames. This update allows BSUIDs to appear in API responses and events, updates the user identity model, and ensures message processing when phone numbers are unavailable. See Migrating your WhatsApp integration to BSUID.
  • Admins can now use admin copilot to manage messaging triggers using natural language prompts. Copilot drafts or modifies the configurations for your review before any changes are finalized. See About admin copilot.
  • Agents can exclude specific tickets from the auto-capacity release timer and messaging inactivity reminders. When automatic capacity release is turned on by an admin, a new Pause messaging reminders standard ticket field can be added to ticket forms and applied to tickets in the Agent Workspace, giving teams greater control over complex messaging conversations. See Automatically releasing agent capacity for inactive conversations and Editing ticket forms.
  • Agents can more easily apply templates to WhatsApp messages after the 24-hour messaging period ends. Approved templates are automatically added to the WhatsApp templates page in Admin Center, and are immediately available to agents in the Agent Workspace. A new countdown clock lets them monitor how much time they have before the 24-hour window closes. See Using templates in WhatsApp conversations.

Contact Center

  • Contact Center now supports agent-first callbacks. Customers can leave the queue without losing their place, and when it’s their turn, Contact Center offers the callback to an available agent before dialing the customer. Admins configure callbacks in Amazon Connect. See Amazon's doc Set up queued callback by creating flows, queues, and routing profiles.

  • Native Zendesk Contact Center now supports agents working in multiple browser tabs or windows. When a call comes in, it rings and displays in each open tab, but Contact Center creates only one ticket for the call. This helps prevent duplicate tickets, reduce agent confusion, and improve reporting accuracy. No action is required.

Voice

  • Zendesk Voice admins with the Copilot add-on can now add call transcripts and AI summaries as collapsible comments instead of internal notes. This helps reduce ticket clutter and makes conversations easier to read. This setting applies only to future calls. Existing transcripts and summaries remain in their original format. To use this option, select Add transcript and summary as collapsible comments in your call transcription settings. 

Analytics

  • The real-time monitoring assistant now features conversational commands that let supervisors take action directly from the monitoring workspace. See Managing tickets and agents using the real-time monitoring assistant.
  • Customizable columns and filters in search results now supports adding custom fields, expanding beyond the previous limitation to standard fields only. This enhancement is available to all Support or Suite plans. See Announcing customizable columns in search results and Announcing customizable filters for advanced search.

Workforce management

  • The automatic agent status updates in Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM) now offer new admin controls to customize when tracked activities from the Zendesk WFM Chrome extension update agent statuses. Admins can enable or disable updates globally, per URL mapping, or for unmapped URLs, allowing more flexible tracking without unintended status changes. See Tracking agent time spent outside of Zendesk.

Quality assurance

  • The Reviewer QA assignments and dashboard feature in Zendesk QA introduces automated, randomized evaluations of reviewers to improve accuracy and consistency. It provides leads and managers with detailed performance insights and supports unbiased, data-driven quality assurance. See Setting up reviewer QA assignments and Reviewer QA dashboard.

Apps and integrations

  • More granular OAuth client scopes introduces finer control over OAuth client permissions by allowing admins to configure allowed scopes in Admin Center. This enhances security by applying the principle of least privilege and expanding available OAuth scopes. See Using OAuth authentication with your application.

  • Action flow connectors are now managed in a dedicated segment of the Zendesk Marketplace, featuring over 50 new connectors, including Slack and Microsoft Teams, plus a new MCP Client and enhanced Marketplace UI for seamless workflow integration.

  • New action builder connectors for ClickUp and Magento 2 enable teams to automate workflows by integrating project management and ecommerce operations with Zendesk support. These connectors allow creating and updating tasks in ClickUp and accessing ecommerce data in Magento 2 directly within action flows. See Using ClickUp actions in action flows and Using Magento 2 actions in action flows.

  • The Connections page in Admin Center centralizes all external system connections in one place, allowing setup, review, and maintenance without switching products. It features a unified list, connector library, search, detailed connection info, and seamless reconnection. Existing connections migrate automatically. See Creating connections to integrate with external services.

  • The MCP client is now generally available. Admins can connect their Zendesk account to public and private MCP servers to make their MCP tools available for use in action flows. This streamlines data fetching and actions in external systems across AI-powered features. See Connecting to MCP servers and using MCP tools in action flows.
  • The App framework for custom object records is now generally available, allowing developers to build contextual sidebar applications directly on Custom object record pages within the Zendesk Agent Workspace. This enables tailored experiences for various business entities and seamless workflows, reducing context switching for agents. See Custom object sidebar apps and Custom object record sidebar for more details.

Employee services

  • Custom tasks and task lists make it possible for agents and admins to create and add custom tasks and task lists directly within tickets without admin setup. This enhances flexibility in tracking ticket-specific actions and integrates with automated workflows. See Using task lists within tickets.
  • Admins can customize ITAM asset fields, including reordering asset fields per asset type, hiding standard asset fields from agent views, and using asset events as action flow triggers. Additionally, the Purchase cost field type changes from decimal to currency, reflecting the account's billing currency. See Reordering asset fields and Hiding unused standard asset fields.
  • New standard user fields for employees for Employee Service Suite plans are: Job Title, Manager, and Team—automatically added to every user record on Employee Service Suite plans. These fields streamline workflows like approval routing, IT asset tracking, and HR integrations. See About user fields.
  • Existing tickets can now be converted to service catalog requests, allowing agents and business rules to associate tickets from any channel with service catalog items using the Service ticket field. This streamlines triage workflows and automates classification of service requests. See Converting tickets to service requests.

articles.name: Testing a voice AI agent
articles.title: Testing a voice AI agent
articles.body:
You can test a voice AI agent in production or sandbox environments in two ways:

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support with Talk Team, Professional, or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

You can test a voice AI agent in production or sandbox using the call console or the browser-based testing widget. The call console checks the full voice experience, including ticket creation, recordings, escalation, transcripts, summaries, and ticket field updates. The testing widget is for live conversation testing only and does not create tickets, support escalation, or test individual procedures.

You can test a voice AI agent in production or sandbox environments in two ways:

  • Use the call console in Agent Workspace to place a test call to the voice line connected to the AI agent. This method tests the complete voice experience, including ticket creation and escalation to a human agent. A test call incurs charges, see About voice AI agents.
  • Use the browser-based testing widget in the AI agents workspace to have a voice conversation directly with the AI agent. The testing widget doesn’t create a ticket or call recording, doesn’t support escalation to a human agent, and can’t test an individual procedure. Testing with the widget doesn’t incur charges.

During testing, verify that the AI agent recognizes expected customer requests, follows the correct procedures, performs configured actions, and responds naturally. When testing with the call console, also verify that the AI agent escalates calls appropriately.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Testing a voice AI agent using the call console
  • Testing a voice AI agent using the testing widget

Testing a voice AI agent using the call console

Use the call console to place a live test call and verify the complete voice AI agent experience.

To test a voice AI agent using the call console

  1. Use the call console in Agent Workspace to call the line connected to the voice AI agent.
  2. Interact with the AI agent as a customer would.
  3. To test your escalation flow, use a second device or an incognito browser to receive handoffs.
  4. After the call, review the resulting ticket to verify the transcript, summary, any available recording, and any ticket field updates made by the AI agent.

Testing a voice AI agent using the testing widget

Use the testing widget to test a voice conversation with your AI agent without placing a live call.

To test a voice AI agent using the testing widget

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.

    Use the case-insensitive literal search to narrow the list of AI agents by name.

  2. Click Test AI agent in the top bar.

    Test your AI agent opens.

  3. (Optional) Select the language for the test from the language menu, if available.
  4. Click Start call.

  5. Have a conversation with the agent by speaking into your microphone.
  6. (Optional) Click the Mute microphone icon () to stop the AI agent from hearing you.
  7. (Optional) Click the Restart conversation icon () or the End call icon () to end the call.

    You can start a new call for another test.

  8. Click the Close icon () to finish testing.

articles.name: Overwrite Tags action fail to work on tickets
articles.title: Overwrite Tags action fail to work on tickets
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

The action Overwrite Tags does not work in Sunshine Conversations and my AI agent. Tags carry over from one ticket and conversation to the next. How do I avoid this situation? This issue confuses my reporting.

Resolution steps

Because the Overwrite action is set to replace tags with ai_agent_start_conversation at the Conversation started event, any session-specific tags added during the flow might remain on the conversation after that session ends.

To clear old tags, keep session tags, and control escalation routing:

  1. At conversation start, run Overwrite conversation tags with a space or blank first to clear inherited tags such as active_incident
  2. Immediately after or at the escalation point in the flow, run Add conversation tags to apply session-relevant tags such as bot_handled. This ensures only intentional tags are present from the start.
  3. If the issue persists, create a configured action using the Sunshine Conversations CRM target and set the task to Clear cached conversation. Add this action at the bot level and set it to trigger on the Session ended event, which fires when the conversation ends, an escalation attempt happens, or the conversation reaches the end of the session duration.
  4. If you expect an agent to use a macro to overwrite tags, ensure the custom role permission linked to the agent has Edit ticket tags enabled.

Following these steps ensures that:

  • Old tags do not bleed into new conversations, and bot_handled is set correctly for reporting and routing.
  • The escalation tag is applied only at the right moment, not inherited from a previous session.
  • You clear the conversation data saved in the session cache within AI agents and force a fresh retrieval of conversation fields at the start of the next session. Tags should not persist on the new ticket after the session ends.

articles.name: With AI agents, my API parameter doesn't store information
articles.title: With AI agents, my API parameter doesn't store information
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

With AI agents, my API parameter doesn't store information. The variable isn't stored, and it removes the variable. I use this procedure: Get Product Details [Dev]. The key 'product_detail' isn't saved, or it's overwritten with the product URL.

When running an API integration and setting a 'Key' or 'Parameter' via JSONata, is that stored automatically when using a procedure, or do I need to add it explicitly within the procedure to Collect parameter? Each time I try to collect the specific parameter to ensure it's stored, it creates an action to map to a new parameter. It doesn't set the parameter, even if the API runs successfully.

Resolution steps

No, a parameter isn't always stored automatically just because the API call succeeds. Request parameters send data to the API, but aren't stored for later steps.

To collect a parameter from an entity:

  1. Use Entity Recognized with your Customer Message blocks

  2. To use Entity Recognized as an input to an API call or within a conditional block further down the dialog, use Collect parameter and save that parameter under its name

For more information, see:

  • Managing generative procedures for AI agents

  • Creating dialogues to define scripted conversation flows for AI agents

Answer

Yes, you can control whether the attachment button appears in the composer from Admin Center.

To turn on or turn off attachments in messaging:

  1. In Admin Center, click Channels in the sidebar, then select Messaging and social > Messaging
  2. Click your Android channel
  3. Click the Style tab and scroll to the bottom

articles.name: Zendesk certification FAQ
articles.title: Zendesk certification FAQ
articles.body:
Overview

A Zendesk certification is a professional credential that validates your expertise with Zendesk products and tools. It’s a valuable career achievement that helps you demonstrate job-ready skills, strengthen your professional profile, and pursue new opportunities in customer experience.

This article covers:

  • Certifications
  • Certification exam results and badges
  • Academy platform
  • Enrollment

Certifications

Can I retake a certification exam?

Yes. Each retake requires a new purchase at the current exam price.

How long is a Zendesk certification valid?

Zendesk certifications are valid for two years. After that, you must repurchase and retake the exam to recertify.

Are certification exams available in other languages?

Yes, some exams are available in other languages. Use the language filters in the certification catalog on Zendesk Academy to see the available options.

Certification exam results and badges

Why didn't I receive my certification exam results or badge?

Results and badges can take up to 72 hours to be issued after an exam. If you still do not see an update after 72 hours, contact academy@zendesk.com with your name, Academy email, and the exam you took.

Why did I receive an error after taking my certification exam?

In most cases, this means the proctoring system flagged the session for review. Contact academy@zendesk.com for further investigation.

I can't find my badge after passing a certification exam. How can I fix it?

If you are not seeing your badge after passing the exam, contact academy@zendesk.com.

Academy platform

I can't log in to my Academy account. What should I do?

The Academy login is different from your Zendesk login. Click Forgot password? in the sign in modal of the Academy and follow the instructions.

Can users host Zendesk Academy content on their own learning platform?

No, it’s not possible to host Zendesk Academy outside the Zendesk environment.

Can admins track their team's learning activity on Academy?

This is not available in a self-serve way. Work with your CSM or contact academy@zendesk.com for static updates.

Enrollment

My promo code isn't working. What should I do?

Contact academy@zendesk.com with the promo code. The team will check whether the code has expired, was already used, or applies only to a specific course or exam language.

Can I get a refund?

Refunds are reviewed on a case-by-case basis and not guaranteed. Email academy@zendesk.com with the reason for your request, and the team will guide you through the next steps.

articles.name: Customizing an AI agent’s opening and closing lines in email responses
articles.title: Customizing an AI agent’s opening and closing lines in email responses
articles.body:
You can customize opening and closing lines for your AI agent's email responses. The customized text is sent exactly as written. It isn't generated, translated, or modified by the AI agent, and it isn't affected by the AI agent'sinstructionsor otherpersonalization settings, including tone of voice or pronoun formality.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise
This article applies only to email AI agents with agentic AI.

You can customize opening and closing lines for your AI agent's email responses. The customized text is sent exactly as written. It isn't generated, translated, or modified by the AI agent, and it isn't affected by the AI agent's instructions or other personalization settings, including tone of voice or pronoun formality.

If you don’t customize specific opening and closing lines, the AI agent uses AI-generated text for its openings and closings.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Customizing an AI agent’s opening and closing lines
  • Using AI-generated opening and closing lines

Customizing an AI agent’s opening and closing lines

You can customize the opening and closing lines of email responses by creating templates for each language you support.

Keep the following limitations in mind:

  • The email footer remains static and can't be edited.
  • Templates aren't translated automatically. You provide your own version of each template for every language you support.
  • Templates are fixed strings. The AI agent doesn't adjust their grammar, so languages with gender- or case-sensitive forms (such as the vocative case in Polish) may need wording that avoids inflected names.

To customize an AI agent's email opening and closing lines

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Content in the sidebar, then select Email content.
  3. Click Manage languages in the upper-right to select one of the supported languages you’ve added.
  4. Click Opening line and enter the text the AI agent should use at the beginning of each email response.

    Optionally, you can personalize the text with the customer’s name. Place the cursor where you want to insert the name, type a forward slash (/), and select one of the following options:

    • customerFirstName
    • customerLastName
    • customerFullName

    Note: If your AI agent was created before July 30, 2026, see Populating the customer name variables for an additional step required to use the customer name variables listed above.
    Alternatively, leave the field empty to use an AI-generated opening line.
  5. Click Closing line and enter the text the AI agent should use at the end of each email response.

    Optionally, you can personalize the text with the customer’s name, as described above.

    Alternatively, leave the field empty to use an AI-generated opening line.
  6. Click Save.
  7. In the Languages panel, click the options menu () for the language you’re customizing and select Enable.

Using AI-generated opening and closing lines

You can configure your AI agent to use AI-generated opening and closing lines, instead of specifically customized ones.

You can do this by leaving the fields blank when you customize the opening and closing lines, or by disabling opening and closing line customizations for a language altogether.

You can disable customizations for a language only if you’ve previously enabled them.

To disable opening and closing customizations

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Content in the sidebar, then select Email content.
  3. Click Manage languages in the upper-right to select one of the supported languages you’ve added.
  4. Click the options menu () for the language you want to disable opening and closing customizations for, then select Disable.
